text:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Canary health degraded for /v1/generate (redwood-large-quantized). Elevated 5xx (p50 latency ok, error rate ~8% -> 18% over last 3m). Auto-rollback attempted but no action taken — feature flag gating present. Paging on-call.
lucy: on it. pinging mohit for infra root cause. grabbing runbook.
mohit: looking at infra now. I see spike in grpc pool saturation on canary hosts. Logs show cache miss storms during kv-restore window.
tara: re: feature flags — I can confirm canary_auto_rollback_enabled is OFF for this rollout (experiment gating). product enabled staged rollback gating yesterday.
lucy: ugh. so auto-rollback is intentionally disabled. ok. need manual rollback. who can run traffic-drain? deploy-bot: @lucy run drain --service=canary --percent=100
lucy: running the drain now. command:
```
# drain canary
deployctl drain --service inference-canary --target-percent 0 --reason "health-degraded: elevated 5xx"
```
deploy-bot: drain initiated. draining 12 hosts, ETA ~90s. will update when complete.
mohit: meanwhile I'm pulling stack traces. observed repeated OOM-ish trace in the log collector but container metrics show memory stable. suspect kernel-level pagefaults when kv cache warms.
tara: any config change in the model packaging? yesterday's change toggled async_kv_restore=true for faster coldstart — could be thrashing.
lucy: good context. @support-jake start prepped customer comms drafts in #support. Which customers hit the 5xx?
support-jake: scaling logs -> 17 unique API keys with >5% errors. top affected: acme-inc (500 errors spike), synth-saas (failed streams). Drafting email and status.io note. will post ASSESSMENT in 10m.
mohit: drain completed - all canary traffic at 0%. Observed error rate drop to baseline on prod routes that had small spillover. But some backend hosts still returning 500s for replayed requests to canary subset.
lucy: initiating manual rollback to previous model tag. command:
```
# rollback model
deployctl promote --service inference-hosted --model-tag redwood-large-2026-02-18 --from=canary
```
deploy-bot: promotion job queued. canary (~12 hosts) will be replaced over rolling windows. Expect full rollback in 4m.
tara: to confirm, promotion will also flip feature flag for canary=false? we should not re-enable auto rollback yet.
mohit: watching host metrics. KV restore storms stop as hosts return to previous model binary. Memory/GC metrics normalize.
ellen: product note: we intentionally gated auto rollback due to wanting manual verification for quantized builds. We should revisit that policy — maybe allow auto-rollback when error rate >10% for 3m.
lucy: agreed. after we stabilize, open follow-up for flag policy. For now, verify correctness.
deploy-bot: rollback promotion finished on 12/12 hosts. traffic normalized. Observed 5xx back to baseline within 90s post-promotion.
support-jake: status note posted: "Partial outage for some customers due to canary model degradation. Rollback completed, mitigation in place. Ops investigating root cause." Link: https://status.example.com/incidents/INC-2026-042
mohit: collecting artifacts for postmortem: kernel logs, kv metrics, packaging diff between tags. starting upload to /mnt/incident-artifacts/1764321987.tar.gz
lucy: handing off to next on-call @sre-rotation. Summary: canary model redwood-large-quantized caused elevated 5xx; auto-rollback blocked by canary_auto_rollback_enabled=false; manual drain + promote performed; customer impact limited to 17 API keys; rollback verified and traffic normalized. Next: investigate kv restore behavior and consider safe auto-rollback thresholds.
sre-rotation: taking this. will run deeper perf tests on quantized build in staging and open FR for flag change.
ellen: I'll sync with product + release to update rollout checklist and add an explicit gate: if errors >10% for 3m AND affected keys >5, auto-rollback allowed.
lucy: closing thread once postmortem linked. thanks all :) :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident resolved. Closure code: manual_rollback_success. Incident ID: INC-2026-042. Timeline & logs uploaded.
